skill.name: prisma-next-contract
skill.description: Authors and validates Prisma Next contracts in PSL or TypeScript, including models, relations, indexes, extensions, namespaces, policies, and emitted artifacts.
skill.summary: Build and update Prisma Next data contracts with correct configuration and emit workflows.

content.value_statement: Complex Prisma Next contracts can fail when schemas, extensions, and configuration drift. This skill guides contract edits, configuration, diagnostics, and artifact emission.
actual_capabilities: Adds and updates models, fields, relations, indexes, enums, aliases, and value objects.
Authors contracts with Prisma Schema Language or the TypeScript contract builder.
Configures PostgreSQL, Mongo, pgvector, Supabase, and other extension namespaces.
Explains namespaces, cross-contract foreign keys, polymorphism, and control policies.
Diagnoses PN-CLI-4002, PN-CLI-4003, and PN-CLI-4011 contract errors.
Runs the contract emit workflow and checks generated contract artifacts.
limitations: It does not apply database migrations or write application queries.
It does not provide built-in validations, lifecycle callbacks, scopes, or soft deletion.
It cannot infer a field rename without an explicit migration strategy.
Database introspection requires an available database and a valid connection string.

use_cases.title: Extend an application schema
use_cases.description: Add models, relations, constraints, and indexes while preserving the established contract layout.

use_cases.title: Configure database extensions
use_cases.description: Register extension descriptors and use namespaced types such as vectors or encrypted strings.

use_cases.title: Model shared contract spaces
use_cases.description: Define namespaces, external tables, control policies, and cross-contract foreign keys.

prompt_templates.title: Add a model
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a {model_name} model to my Prisma Next contract with these fields: {fields}. Preserve the current authoring format.

prompt_templates.title: Create a relation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a {relation_type} relation between {source_model} and {target_model}. Add explicit referential actions and useful indexes.

prompt_templates.title: Configure an extension
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure {extension_name} for this Prisma Next project and add a field using {extension_type}. Update every required descriptor surface.

prompt_templates.title: Design a contract architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Prisma Next contract for {domain}. Include namespaces, value objects, polymorphism, control policies, and cross-contract references where justified.

output_examples.input: Add posts with authors, unique titles per author, and cascading deletion.
output_examples.output: The contract gains a Post model, an owning author relation, a composite unique constraint, and an author index. Emitted artifacts are refreshed.
The configuration registers the pgvector control descriptor. The contract uses its vector type, and TypeScript authoring registers the matching pack.

output_examples.input: Explain why contract emit returns PN-CLI-4011.
output_examples.output: The contract references an extension namespace that configuration does not register. Add the matching extension descriptor, then emit the contract again.

best_practices: Read prisma-next.config.ts first and edit only the configured contract source.
Use public target and extension facade imports in user-authored files.
Emit after every source change and verify both generated artifacts changed.
anti_patterns: Do not edit contract.json or contract.d.ts because emission replaces manual changes.
Do not use internal Prisma Next package imports from application code.
Do not treat a field rename as a safe automatic drop and add.

faq.question: Which contract formats are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports contract.prisma with Prisma Schema Language and contract.ts with the TypeScript builder.

faq.question: Can it apply migrations?
faq.answer: No. It authors and emits contracts. Use the Prisma Next migrations workflow to plan and apply database changes.

faq.question: Can it work with PostgreSQL and Mongo?
faq.answer: Yes. It selects the matching target facade and respects differences between SQL and Mongo contract features.

faq.question: How are extensions configured?
faq.answer: Configuration uses control descriptors. TypeScript contracts also register pack descriptors in the contract builder.

faq.question: Does it support existing databases?
faq.answer: Yes. Prisma Next can infer a contract from an accessible database before the skill refines and emits it.

faq.question: Does it support automatic rename detection?
faq.answer: No. Renames require a reviewed migration edit or a staged keep-then-drop strategy.
